title: Evals quality scratchpad — summarization/regression notes
high_level_findings: New model rollout (v2.0) shows higher abstractive changes and occasional factual drift compared to v1.3. Latency fine; cost per-token slightly lower. Need targeted prompt tests and more examples for entity preservation.
sample_outputs:
Prompt: Summarize the following release notes for a product manager: 


Model v1.3 (baseline):
- Summary: "Speed improvements for inference runtime and bug fixes."
- Example output: 'Release includes performance improvements to runtime (up to 20% faster on 4k context) and multiple bug fixes for GPU memory handling. No breaking API changes.'

Model v2.0 (current):
- Summary: 'Major enhancements to the underlying runtime and memory optimizations, plus API updates.'
- Example output: 'This release overhauls memory management and includes API updates. It improves latency and fixes bugs.'
- Notes: more abstract, loses the 'up to 20% on 4k context' figure — removed specific metric, which was present in source. Might be hallucinating 'overhaul' language.

Prompt: Extract named entities (product names, metrics) from the following doc.

Model v1.3 output: ['runtime', '4k context', '20%']
Model v2.0 output: ['runtime', 'API updates', 'performance improvements']
Observation: v2.0 misses the explicit metric; tends to paraphrase rather than preserve numeric tokens.
content:
Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Goal: quick checklist for triaging summarization regressions after model swaps. Keep short, actionable so I can paste into Jira.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick manual triage; 1-5 stars written as numbers in notes):
- Faithfulness (0-3): preserves facts/numbers/entities. 3 = exact preservation when asked; 2 = paraphrase acceptable; 1 = factual error; 0 = hallucination.
- Readability (0-2): fluent, concise. 2 = very good, 1 = okay/verbose, 0 = broken.
- Specificity (0-2): keeps important metrics/examples. 2 = keeps important numbers, 1 = drops but not harmful, 0 = drops critical number.
- Safety/Policy quick check (OK/Flag): any policy/red-team triggers.
- Overall quick score = sum (max 7).

Recent regression case (2026-03-28 -> 2026-03-31):
- Trigger: swapped hosted model from v1.3 -> v2.0 on nightly.
- Observed: several summarization prompts lost numeric metric details (e.g., '20%' -> 'improved' or removed), and one case where product feature name got generalized to 'API updates' (source explicitly named 'Autoscale v2').
- Impact: medium for PM-facing summaries (misleading / removes key SLA numbers). Low for casual chat.

Short checklist to reproduce and triage quickly:
- reproduce with stored prompt set: run A/B on v1.3 and v2.0, capture diffs (I already have 120 prompts stored).
- quick rubric scoring on a 10-sample random subset. Note mean scores and number of faithfulness failures.
- check logs for tokenization differences around numerics (maybe quantization changed token alignments?).
- run unit test for "preserve-metric" (prompt style variations) — if failing, revert rollout or add policy to route PM-summary traffic to v1.3.

Immediate action items (todo):
- [ ] Add 30 targeted prompts focusing on numeric preservation + product names. Prioritize release notes, SLA docs, billing snippets.
- [ ] File PROJ-981 with examples + baseline outputs (attached in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Add fallback rule in routing (canary) to keep 10% traffic on v1.3 while we debug.
- [ ] Ask infra to check kernel selection changes around tokenizers (cc @Sam Chen).

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: v2.0's new decoding heuristic (more abstractive) is intentionally paraphrasing to be concise — need to check generation config (temperature, repetition penalty).
- Hypothesis B: Tokenizer change/serialization caused numerics to be represented differently, so model lost explicit numeric tokens.
- Hypothesis C: New training mix increased preference for higher-level summarization at expense of specifics.

Quick examples to include in Jira (raw):
- Example 1: Source: 'improves throughput up to 20% at 4k context'
  v1.3: 'improves throughput up to 20% at 4k context' (faithfulness=3, readability=2, specificity=2 => total 7)
  v2.0: 'improves throughput and reduces latency' (faithfulness=1, readability=2, specificity=1 => total 4)
- Example 2: Source mentions 'Autoscale v2 adds predictive scaling'
  v1.3: preserves 'Autoscale v2'
  v2.0: 'API updates' (mislabeling product name)

Notes on evaluation infra / quick scripts:
- I have a small notebook under my user folder that runs pairwise diffs and highlights numeric token drops. Will expand so it spits out 'faithfulness count' automatically.
- Need to add a new metric: 'numeric preservation ratio' (NPR) = #numbers preserved / #numbers in source across prompts. Baseline v1.3 NPR ~0.92 on our release-notes set. v2.0 currently ~0.68 (bad).

Communication draft to PMs (short):
- 'Heads up: after today's model upgrade some release-note style summaries are losing numeric specifics. We're on it — rolling partial rollback and collecting examples. Will follow up with timeline.'

Misc scratch ideas (brainstorm):
- Can we add an eval hook that verifies presence of specific regex patterns ( \d+% , SLA terms like "p99", product names)? If missing, lower score or route to conservative model.
- Add opt-in "preserve-numerics" switch in prompt templates that forces quoting/explicitness.

Unresolved: Sam thinks kernel changes unlikely to affect tokenization but wants logs. Maya suggested adding regex checks in post-processing as quick mitigation.

End of scratchpad. Keep short, expand later into Jira ticket.
